excerpt: Hex is an AI analytics workspace with SQL and Python notebooks, data apps and a Hex agent. Plans from free to $75 per editor a month, and alternatives.
content:
Hex is a data analytics workspace. Analysts work in notebooks that mix SQL, Python and no-code cells, then publish the results as interactive data apps that colleagues can use without touching code. On top of that sit AI features: a Notebook Agent that can write queries, build charts and draft reports, and Threads, a chat-style way for non-analysts to ask questions of the data themselves. To keep AI answers grounded, Hex uses a context layer built from semantic models and descriptions of your database. Its pricing page says every plan can connect to any data source.

Hex says it supports more than 2,000 customers worldwide. Companies named on its site include Reddit, Notion, Anthropic, Ramp, Rivian, Figma, Cursor, StubHub, Chime, Brex and Mercor. On its homepage, Mercor is quoted as saying the Notebook Agent cut report turnaround from days to hours. The company does not give its founding year or investors on its About page, saying only that it has raised money from investors and is six years in.

Plans and pricing

Hex charges per editor, the people who build notebooks and apps. The free Community plan includes a trial of the Hex agent, any data connection, all cell types and small compute (4 GB memory, half a CPU). Professional costs $36 per editor a month and adds the Hex agent with a standard monthly AI credit grant, up to 5 published apps, 30-day version history and medium compute. Team costs $75 per editor a month with a larger credit grant, unlimited published apps, drill-down exploration, scheduled runs and alerts, and unlimited version history. Enterprise is custom and adds an Explorer seat for people who only explore, audit logs, single sign-on, single-tenant hosting, HIPAA and embedded analytics options.

AI credits are granted per seat each month and do not roll over; Hex does not state the amounts. Larger machines are billed per minute on Team and Enterprise, from $0.32 an hour for Large to $4.06 an hour for an A10G GPU. Team has a free trial, and students and educators can get Professional free.

We have not tested Hex ourselves. This page brings together Hex's official site, its own announcements and reputable news coverage, plus the public pages of the products it is compared with, and says where each fact comes from.

use_cases: Explore warehouse data in a notebook mixing SQL and Python
Publish an interactive data app or dashboard for colleagues
Let business users ask data questions in plain language (Threads)
Have the Notebook Agent draft queries, charts and reports

fit: are a data team that works in SQL and Python and wants to share results as apps
want AI help grounded in your own semantic models
have a small team and want published per-editor prices
not_fit: need lots of viewers who only explore data without paying for editor seats: the Explorer seat is an Enterprise add-on
need SSO or audit logs below Enterprise
only want a free notebook for personal use; open-source Jupyter does that

pros: SQL, Python and no-code in one notebook
Results can be published as interactive apps
Clear per-editor prices for Professional and Team
cons: AI credit amounts per plan are not stated
Single sign-on and audit logs are Enterprise features
Large compute costs extra per minute

pricing.intro: Hex's own prices, in US dollars per editor per month.

plans.name: Community
plans.detail: Hex agent trial, any data source, all cell types, small compute (4 GB, 0.5 CPU)

plans.name: Professional
plans.detail: Hex agent with standard credits, up to 5 published apps, 30-day version history, medium compute

plans.name: Team
plans.detail: Extended credits, unlimited published apps, drill-down exploration, unlimited version history, scheduled runs and alerts

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Explorer seat add-on, premium credits, audit logs, OIDC SSO, BYOK, single-tenant, HIPAA and embedded analytics add-ons, dedicated support

notes: AI credits are granted per seat each month and do not roll over; extra credits can be bought on paid plans.
Pay-as-you-go compute on Team and Enterprise: Large $0.32/hr, XL $0.65/hr, 2XL $1.29/hr, 4XL $2.58/hr, A10G GPU $4.06/hr, L4 GPU $2.93/hr, billed per minute.
Students and educators can get Professional free; non-profits can apply for a discount.

items.name: Jupyter
items.difference: Free and self-run, but without Hex's hosted apps, governance and AI agent.
